notes: Original research article (Full Length Article), not retracted (record.json is_retracted false), no statement that the uptake values were published before. I2 is a judgement: the paper does not report the carbon content of the biochars (Table 1 gives composition of the raw wheat straw only: C 42.30 wt%, ad). Sorbents are 700, 800 and 900 °C pyrolysis chars described as porous biochar with developed micropores (type I isotherm for 900 °C char, Section 3.1), i.e. a carbonized material, so I treated it as a carbon sorbent. If the reviewer requires a stated carbon content for the char, I2 is the criterion at risk. I1: static Sieverts instrument, uptake in mol/kg at 30 °C (vacuum to 70 bar; 700 °C char 0.39 to 1.70 mol/kg at 8.28 to 66.33 bar; 900 °C char max 2.50 mol/kg at 66.33 bar) and at −196 °C for the 900 °C char. I4: the surface areas are from Ar at −185.86 °C (labelled BET*), reported for the same chars used for H2. Internal inconsistency in the paper: abstract gives 15.29 mol/kg at 46.21 bar for the cryogenic maximum, Section 3.4 and Conclusions give 15.59 mol/kg at 46.71 bar; this does not affect eligibility.
